top_stories.title: What is the Tower of Babel? Pope Leo XIV compares AI risk to ancient biblical warning | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Pope Leo XIV** compared the rapid rise of artificial intelligence to the biblical story of the Tower of Babel, warning against unchecked ambition and technological progress without ethical responsibility.  He cited the story's message about human pride and the dangers of pursuing power without wisdom as a cautionary tale for the development of AI. The Pope expressed concerns that uncontrolled AI could lead to confusion, inequality, and social division if not developed with ethical safeguards and human oversight.

top_stories.title: Police arrest suspect in killing of newly married couple in Karachi's Malir: spokesperson - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Saudabad police** arrested the main suspect, Sajid, son of Aslam, in connection with the shooting death of a newly married couple near RCD ground in Malir's Saudabad. The suspect confessed to opening fire on the couple after they returned from court where the woman had recorded her statement about marrying willingly.  A case was registered at Saudabad police station based on the complaint of the deceased husband’s brother, and raids are underway to arrest other suspects involved.

top_stories.title: Ebola in DR Congo: Fast response needed to stop 'catastrophe', DR Congo governor sayss
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Democratic Republic of Congo**'s Ituri province, the epicenter of a current Ebola outbreak, is facing dire conditions as officials struggle to contain the spread. Governor Johnny Luboya Nkashama has called for increased resources and personnel to prevent further catastrophe, highlighting issues such as food shortages and overcrowding. The **World Health Organization (WHO)** declared a public health emergency of international concern, emphasizing the need for swift action.  The outbreak, which has already claimed over 200 lives, is spreading beyond Ituri province into neighboring Uganda and other parts of the region.

top_stories.title: Labor to announce easing of jobseeker mutual obligations requirements in major overhaul of employment system | Unemployment | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Amanda Rishworth**, the **Australian** Minister for Social Services, will outline plans to overhaul the country's employment system.  She is expected to criticize the current mutual obligation regime as "ill-equipped" and ineffective in helping unemployed Australians find work.  Rishworth will propose a new model with three streams of support tailored to individual needs, aiming to address concerns about unfairness and inadequate job placement assistance. The government plans to engage in consultation on the proposed changes before finalizing them.

top_stories.title: Tehran labels US attacks ‘gross violation’, says it is prepared to respond | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The US** carried out strikes against Iranian targets in the southern province of Hormozgan, shortly after both sides indicated progress in peace talks. **Iran's** foreign ministry condemned the attacks as a "gross violation" of the fragile ceasefire and said it is prepared to respond. The commander of the **Revolutionary Guard's Aerospace Force**, **Seyed Majid Moosavi**, criticized ongoing diplomacy, stating that negotiations with the enemy are "pure loss."  The US Secretary of State, **Marco Rubio**, stated that the Strait of Hormuz must be open "one way or the other," while **Iran** has been allowing some ships through. The attacks come amid intense negotiations between **Iran** and the **US** for a memorandum of understanding to halt the war and restart shipping through the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

top_stories.title: Sebi chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey backs bond ETFs, tokenisation as debt fundraising nears Rs 9 lakh crore - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Sebi** chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey highlighted the growing importance of India's debt market, noting that it has raised nearly Rs 9 lakh crore in FY26, almost double the amount raised by the equity market.  He emphasized the need for deeper development of the corporate bond market to support long-term economic growth and urged greater retail participation and reduced dependence on bank-led financing. **Sebi** is exploring initiatives such as bond ETFs, stronger disclosures, tokenization pilots, and outreach programs to improve investor awareness and accessibility in fixed-income products.  Pandey stressed that regulation must evolve with market structures and emerging risks.

top_stories.title: UDF will clarify stance on PM SHRI soon: Minister - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala will clarify its stance on the PM SHRI scheme soon.**  Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen stated that the UDF, which succeeded the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government, is seeking legal advice to determine if it can withdraw from the agreement unilaterally and what impact such a withdrawal would have. The UDF opposes the scheme due to its federal principles concerns and content disagreements.  The UDF leadership will make a decision based on all aspects of the issue.

top_stories.title: DOWN THE RABBIT HOLE: Pope Leo's Tower of Babel warning for artificial intelligence pits new gods against old ones | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIII issued his first encyclical, titled "Magnifica Humanitas," warning of the dangers of Artificial Intelligence. He compares AI to the Tower of Babel, a biblical allegory that warns against human ambition and attempts to reach heaven without God's blessing. The Pope argues that technology can dehumanize humanity if it prioritizes efficiency over compassion and ignores the importance of human connection.  He believes that AI should be developed with ethical considerations in mind, ensuring that it does not replace or diminish human dignity.

top_stories.title: Jail authorities request medical examination of alleged drug queenpin Anmol over kidney pain - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Central jail authorities in Karachi requested the Civil Hospital to send a medical team to examine Anmol alias Pinky, an alleged drug queenpin, for kidney issues.** **The jail superintendent** cited security concerns as the reason for not transporting her to the hospital.  The examining physician recommended further evaluation and tests at the Sindh Institute of Urology & Transplantation (SIUT). The police also requested treatment within the prison premises.

top_stories.title: Eleven killed in east Lebanon village as Israel intensifies strikes
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Israel** intensified its military action against **Hezbollah** in southern and eastern Lebanon, targeting over 100 sites following a vow by **Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu** to increase the intensity of strikes. The attacks resulted in the deaths of eleven people, including two children, in the village of Mashghara.  The Israeli military claimed to have eliminated terrorists at the targeted sites while also striking weapons storage facilities and other infrastructure used by **Hezbollah**.  **Hezbollah**, in response, launched rockets and drones at northern Israel.
